Clean one day of LOBSTER data

Source: R/clean.R
lobster_clean.Rd

Reads one day's message file and order book file, keeps the messages of continuous trading and returns one row per message with the book state after it. The order book is read block by block (or level by level from parquet) and only as deep as the depth measures need, so even a 100-level file of a very active stock never has to fit into memory. Files can be read straight from a LOBSTER .7z archive without unpacking it.

Usage

lobster_clean(
  message_file,
  orderbook_file,
  archive = NULL,
  ticker = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  trading_hours = c("09:30:00", "16:00:00"),
  depth_bp = c(0, 5),
  cut_at_crosses = TRUE,
  block_size = 2^27
)

Arguments

message_file, orderbook_file

character(1) The day's message file and order book file: paths to CSV files (also .csv.gz), or member names inside archive. The order book can also be a parquet file whose columns follow LOBSTER's order (needs the 'nanoparquet' package).

archive

character(1) or NULL Path to a LOBSTER .7z archive that holds the two files. They are streamed from the archive; nothing is unpacked to disk. The 7z program is used when it is installed (it is faster), the 'archive' package otherwise; set options(lobsteR.use_7z = FALSE) to always use 'archive'.

ticker, date

Ticker and trading day. By default parsed from the file names.

trading_hours

character(2) or numeric(2) Start and end of the continuous session in New York time, as "HH:MM", "HH:MM:SS" or seconds after midnight. Defaults to 09:30–16:00; use c("09:30", "13:00") on early-close days or a wider window for pre- and post-market trading (together with cut_at_crosses = FALSE).

depth_bp

numeric Distances from the best price, in basis points, for which depth is computed. 0 gives the size at the best price. NULL reads only the best level.

cut_at_crosses

logical(1) Start continuous trading after the opening cross and end it before the closing cross when they fall inside trading_hours.

block_size

numeric(1) Bytes of CSV text parsed at a time. Each block passes through one temporary file in tempdir(), which is overwritten block by block and removed at the end. Larger blocks are slightly faster and use more memory.

Value

A data.table with one row per message of continuous trading (types 1 to 5) and columns

ts

seconds after midnight, New York time, as in LOBSTER.

time

the same instant as POSIXct in America/New_York.

type, order_id, size, direction

as in the message file.

price

message price in USD.

trade_sign

+1 buyer-, -1 seller-initiated, 0 unsigned; NA for messages that are not executions.

midpoint

TRUE for hidden executions exactly at the midquote before the trade.

best_ask, best_bid, midquote

in USD, after the message.

spread

quoted spread in basis points of the midquote.

depth{bp}_ask, depth{bp}_bid

shares within bp basis points of the best price, for each value of depth_bp.

depth{bp}_truncated

for each positive bp: depth may be cut short by the number of levels in the file.

Midquote and spread are NA when the book is crossed or one side is empty. Depth is NA only in crossed books; an empty side has depth 0. The attribute "lobster" holds the day's metadata, the crosses, the halts, the book states at the session boundaries and a log of dropped messages; lobster_snapshots() needs it, and lobster_crosses(), lobster_halts() and lobster_log() read it.

Cleaning steps

  1. Book state. Prices stay in LOBSTER's integer units (USD x 10000) for all comparisons. Dummy prices (ask 9999999999, bid -9999999999) mark empty levels. A book state is valid when both sides are non-empty and the best ask is not below the best bid; otherwise midquote and spread are NA. In a one-sided book the empty side has depth 0; in a crossed book all book variables are NA.

  2. Depth. For each distance in depth_bp, the number of shares at the levels priced within that many basis points of the best price on each side (not of the midquote). depth0 is the size at the best price. depth{bp}_truncated flags rows where the deepest level in the file still lies inside the distance, so that depth may be cut short by the number of levels requested from LOBSTER.

  3. Trading hours and crosses. Messages outside trading_hours (New York time) are dropped. With cut_at_crosses = TRUE, continuous trading starts after the opening cross (type 6, order id -1) and ends before the closing cross (type 6, order id -2) whenever these lie inside the trading hours. All crosses are reported, with price and volume, in lobster_crosses(), and never enter the cleaned messages.

  4. Halts. Type 7 messages are paired by their price field: a halt (price -1) lasts until the next resumption of trading (price 1) or the next execution, whichever comes first (some files hold halt messages without a resumption on days that trade normally); resumption of quoting (price 0) does not end it. Halts are found in the full message stream before any time filter, so a halt that starts before the open still ends at its resumption. A halt without resumption lasts until the close. Messages during halts are dropped; the halts are listed in lobster_halts().

  5. Trade direction. trade_sign is +1 for buyer-initiated and -1 for seller-initiated trades. Visible executions (type 4) take the opposite of LOBSTER's direction, which is the side of the resting order. Hidden executions (type 5) carry no usable direction in the NASDAQ feed, so they are signed against the midquote just before the trade: the book state after the previous message of the full stream, compared in integer units (2 * price against ask + bid). Hidden trades exactly at that midquote (typically midpoint-peg orders) get trade_sign = 0 and midpoint = TRUE; hidden trades without a valid quote before them also get 0.

See also

lobster_snapshots() to aggregate to a regular time grid, lobster_process() to do both in one step.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
msgs <- lobster_clean(
  "SPY_2024-03-20_34200000_57600000_message_50.csv",
  "SPY_2024-03-20_34200000_57600000_orderbook_50.csv"
)
lobster_crosses(msgs)

# straight from the archive, early close
msgs <- lobster_clean(
  "AAPL_2024-11-29_34200000_46800000_message_10.csv",
  "AAPL_2024-11-29_34200000_46800000_orderbook_10.csv",
  archive = "AAPL_2024-11-01_2024-11-29_10.7z",
  trading_hours = c("09:30", "13:00")
)
} # }
